title: Pneumatic — Replacement of the Bleed Isolation Valve Actuator and Position Regulator
abstract: Retrofit of the low-temperature bleed isolation valve actuator and its matched position regulator on aircraft delivered before the production cut-in, aimed at operators in cold climates.

sections.planning_reason: Twenty-nine occurrences of a slow bleed isolation valve were recorded on cold-soaked aircraft over two northern winters, nine of which produced a bleed configuration caution that had to be cleared before departure. The valve took between eleven and eighteen seconds to reach the commanded position against a design figure of four. Operators outside cold climates are unlikely to see the condition, which is why the bulletin is recommended rather than mandatory.
sections.description: The bulletin replaces the isolation valve actuator with a unit built with a low-temperature grease and a higher stall torque, replaces the matched position regulator, and changes the duct clamp arrangement between the valve and the cross-bleed duct.
sections.accomplishment_summary: Open the fan cowl and get access to the isolation valve in the pylon area. Disconnect the electrical connector at the actuator. Remove the actuator and the position regulator GIR634074-45. Install the new position regulator D3610120750241 and torque to the value in the task. Install the low-temperature actuator on the valve body D3610116310629 and set the null position with the rigging pin. Install the cushioned clamps EN984959K3 at the duct joint and fit new swaged collars EN767708K2. Do the installation task AMM-C-36-10-12-400-012-A and then a valve travel test at ambient temperature. Repeat on the other side. Close the fan cowl and record the embodiment.
sections.effectivity_note: Applicable to CIRRANE-11 and CIRRANE-13 aircraft from MSN C00001 to MSN C00205 that carry the delivered actuator standard. It does not apply to aircraft already brought to the four-position standard, on which the actuator is common and the wiring differs. One prototype aircraft is excluded.
sections.material_note: Kit K3610-2002-01 contains two actuators, two regulators, four clamps and the collar set. Lead time is twelve weeks. Removed actuators are returned for teardown for the first twenty embodiments and may be scrapped locally thereafter.

type_data.compliance_time: Within twenty-four months for operators whose network includes airfields where the aircraft is regularly cold-soaked below minus twenty degrees Celsius; at the operator's convenience otherwise.
